About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using.

Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors.

This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

What You'll Be Responsible For

•
Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python.

•
Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list.

•
Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope.

•
Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases.

•
Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it.

•
Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics.

•
Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog.

•
Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump.

•
Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents, which are now a major consumer of it.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

•
Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any.

•
Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on.

•
Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked.

•
Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers.

•
Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml, wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly.

•
Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test.

•
Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default.

•
Have real autonomy: you find the important work, scope it, ship it, and say what you didn't do.

•
Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences

•
Have experience in async or globally distributed teams

•
Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers

•
Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly

Bonus points if you: have run a major-version migration for a public package, know your way around JWT/OAuth, have built integrations for AI agent frameworks, or have generated idiomatic clients from a schema.

What We Offer

•
Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•
ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•
Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•
Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•
~400 team members

•
60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

listing.description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

• Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
• Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
• Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
• Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
• Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
• Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
• Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.

Requirements

• 2+ years of professional software engineering
• Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
• Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
• Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
• Regular use of an AI coding tool
• Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
• You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
• At least 10 hours a week, starting now
• A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)

Nice to have

• Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
• Experience building agent tasks or RL environments

Terms

• US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
• Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
• The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
• Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform that 10M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime and Vector Search all run on one platform: the same compute, the same disks, the same network and control plane, in every region we operate.

Supabase's hardest problems live in that platform. Millions of databases, growth that compounds every quarter, and a customer base running from a developer on a free project to a regulated enterprise routing traffic through PrivateLink. Reliability, capacity, cost and the enterprise features that close deals all come back to the same primitives. We're hiring a Product Lead to own them.

About the role

You own the platform primitives every Supabase product runs on: compute, disks, networking, the API gateway, capacity and regions. You own the enterprise surfaces built on top of them too, including read replicas, custom domains, PrivateLink and Bring Your Own Cloud. You report to the Head of Product and set direction for the whole area alongside the leads for our other product lines. You're the only product person on the platform today, and the team grows under you as the area does.

What you'll be responsible for:

•

You talk to customers across the full spectrum. Developers running a single small project, growing startups whose bill is mostly compute and disk, enterprises walking through a network architecture review, and partners building on top of Supabase.

•

You own the problem statement and requirements behind every platform bet. You define what we're building and why before engineering starts, name the cost, capacity and reliability constraints, and keep that clarity current through execution.

•

You decide what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets cut. Every quarter you're choosing between enterprise unlocks that open new markets, cost and performance wins for the long tail of projects, and net-new capabilities that change what Supabase can run. The priorities are yours, and so is defending them.

•

You own reliability as a product surface. You set service levels that track what customers experience, hold teams to them, and show customers what it takes to run millions of databases.

•

You define how each launch is measured before it ships. The metric, the threshold and the read afterwards are yours: whether a launch moved enterprise deal velocity, project economics, or platform reliability.

•

You keep engineering, design and leadership aligned. The platform touches every other Supabase product, every region and every customer tier. You write down what's coming, why, and in what order, and you surface dependencies before they become blockers.

You might be a good fit if you:

•

Have 8+ years of product management experience on developer tools, or are an ex-founder who has built in this space. You're technical enough to read an architecture doc and follow a design discussion.

•

Have shipped cloud infrastructure as a product. You've owned at least one of compute, networking, storage, or multi-region and multi-tenant systems at a cloud, infrastructure or PaaS company, as the owner rather than a neighbouring team. You can judge the tradeoffs: instance sizing and capacity, disk and storage economics, scale-to-zero versus always-on, single-tenant versus shared, and the distance between "works in one region" and "works in twenty." Familiarity with how enterprises buy infrastructure (PrivateLink, BYOC, procurement) is a bonus.

•

Have grown with an infrastructure product. You've owned infrastructure small enough to hold in your head, and stayed with it until capacity, regions and cost became the real constraints.

•

Are biased toward speed. You'd rather ship something imperfect and learn from it.

•

Build with what you own. You stand up a read replica, put a custom domain in front of a project, terminate traffic through PrivateLink, deploy onto BYOC. You develop opinions through first-hand use.

•

Use AI to move faster. You lean on AI for the slow parts of the job (research, drafting, synthesising feedback) so you spend more time on judgment calls.

•

Work async by default. We're fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

About us

IOMETE is the sovereign data platform for the AI era. Enterprises run our data lakehouse, built on Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg, in their own trusted environment: on-premises, in their own cloud, or hybrid. It is built for regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare and government. Customer data never leaves the customer's trust perimeter, and the AI we build on it stays inside that perimeter too.

Position overview

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated AI Software Engineer to join our team. We tackle a variety of exciting challenges, from connecting AI tools and models to the lakehouse to diagnosing Spark applications and troubleshooting failures. You'll build agents that run inside the customer's environment, on LLMs the customer provides or, later, on custom models we train for Spark tuning and troubleshooting. You'll also build the framework that defines those agents and the harness that runs, limits, traces and evaluates them.

The AI team

We are building the AI platform for the lakehouse — Lakehouse Intelligence. The team's roadmap includes, but is not limited to, the MCP Server for AI Agents, which lets AI tools query the lakehouse; the Model Gateway, through which IOMETE's AI features call models; agents for Spark application diagnosis, troubleshooting and onboarding; and SQL AI Functions, which run language models from inside a query. Down the road, you'll also get to fine-tune and build custom models for our platform's specific needs, small enough to run inside a customer's deployment.

What you'll do

•
Contribute to and maintain IOMETE's AI services, including the MCP Server for AI Agents, the Model Gateway, SQL AI Functions, and lakehouse-specific agents (such as Spark Application Diagnosis) and their harness.

•
Build AI enablers: extend the IOMETE lakehouse and platform to support more AI-powered features, for example by making Spark job logs, query history and table metadata available to them.

•
Be hands-on with Kubernetes, including the Helm charts that ship our AI services into each customer's deployment.

•
Collaborate closely with external customer engineering teams to support integrations, troubleshoot complex issues and provide guidance for successful adoption of our platform.

•
Participate in design discussions about agents, model access, evaluation, and overall systems architecture.

•
Write the tests, docs and release notes for what you build. A feature is done when it has shipped with all of them.

•
Review your teammates' work and provide feedback.

What we're looking for

•
5+ years of professional experience in software engineering (we’re open to exceptional candidates with less experience who demonstrate deep systems knowledge and impact).

•
Deep understanding of LLM-based systems in production – tool calling, structured output, retrieval, evaluation, and how they fail.

•
Our AI features are written mostly in Python and Go. The data platform is built on the JVM, in Kotlin and Java, and new platform features are being built in Go. Production experience with any of these languages is a big plus, but we know strong engineers learn a new language fast.

•
Familiarity with distributed systems and their challenges (e.g., data consistency, fault tolerance, scheduling).

•
Fluency in English, both written and verbal — this role involves working with international customers and partners.

•
Based in a time zone that overlaps Amsterdam working hours (CET/CEST).

Preferred qualifications

•

About the Role

We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company.

This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

•
Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. Take ideas from identification through to a realized dollar figure, not just a recommendation.

•
Build and maintain the FinOps data pipeline: Design and run the BigQuery/dbt models that turn raw billing and usage data (CUR, Storage Lens) into reconciled, trustworthy mart tables, the foundation everything else in FinOps is built on.

•
Build cost-vs-revenue and customer segmentation models: Model unit economics and margin by product line and customer segment, and extend coverage as new products and segments come online.

•
Apply data science to cost and usage data: Build forecasting models, detect anomalies statistically rather than by threshold alone, and quantify savings opportunities (e.g. storage lifecycle, request-cost patterns) with rigor a spreadsheet can't match.

•
Build and maintain cost attribution: Tagging policies, cost allocation, and chargeback/showback so engineering teams can see and own their own spend. This is foundational work other savings work depends on.

•
Automate cost governance: Build automated cost reporting, anomaly detection, and alerting. Write the scripts and infrastructure-as-code (Python, Terraform, Lambda) that enforce cost policy rather than relying on manual review.

•
Partner with engineering on architecture decisions: Bring cost into the room early, cost-efficiencies are cheaper to get right at design than to retrofit.

•
Work with Finance on forecasting and reporting: Support budget tracking and financial KPIs; build dashboards and self-serve analytics engineering and finance can both read.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

•
Have strong AWS expertise and working GCP knowledge, including pricing models, billing structures, and cost optimization mechanics.

•
Have data engineering depth: dbt, BigQuery (or an equivalent modern warehouse), SQL at scale, and data modeling for analytics (dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing).

•
Have data science fundamentals: statistical forecasting, anomaly detection, and experimentation, and know when a rigorous model beats a rule of thumb.

•
Have automation and scripting skills: Python, Terraform/ pulumi, Lambda, or Bash.

•
Are comfortable with cost/billing tooling: AWS Cost Explorer, Cost & Usage Reports, GCP Billing Reports, and BI/dashboarding (we use Hex).

•
Have experience with, or are comfortable picking up, Linear and Notion as the system of record for tracking and documenting FinOps work.

•
Experience with a dedicated cloud cost management platform (e.g. CloudZero, Vantage, or similar) is a plus, not required.

•
Can analyze cost data and present it clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

•
Have prior experience spanning data analytics, data engineering, or data science in a FinOps, cloud cost management, or cloud governance context.

•
Are energized by doing the unglamorous, high-leverage work (the schlep) that unblocks other teams, and by working cross-functionally without positional authority.

What We Offer

•
Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•
ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•
Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•
Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•
Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•
Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•
Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•
~400 team members

•
60+ countries

•
20+ languages spoken

•
Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•
540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Headquarters: Remote

You're the detection engineer people turn to when they ask "what does Microsoft actually see here?" Not the marketing-slide answer, the real map. Which product emits which telemetry, any anticipated ingestion lags, what table or API it lands in, which license tier gates it, how long it survives before it ages out, and where the documentation quietly disagrees with reality. When a new technique drops, your first instinct is to ask which Microsoft signal would catch it, and whether customers have it switched on.

You also know Microsoft never sits still. Hunting tables appear, columns get renamed, Graph versions retire, capability shuffles between SKUs, previews go GA, features quietly vanish, and native alert logic shifts underneath you. You've got a repeatable way of staying ahead of that churn instead of finding out when a detection stops firing. You're comfortable behind a command line and in front of a customer, including scenarios where the conversation isn’t pleasant. If that's you, we'd love to talk! We have an amazing team and believe you'll love getting to know us.

At Expel, we help businesses bridge the cybersecurity talent gap by providing transparent Managed Detection and Response. To do this we build technology to make sure our security analysts are solving important problems, and automation is helping them make better decisions at every step. We delight in using technology to make security accessible for our customers.

What Expel can do for you

• Make you one of our recognized authorities on Microsoft detection and response — for our SOC, our engineers, our go-to-market teams, and our customers

• Give you real ownership of Expel's detection coverage across the whole Microsoft security estate

• Put Microsoft telemetry from across our customer base in front of you — a breadth of real-world environments no single enterprise gets to see

• Let you write and tune detections in our own rule engine and watch them run against live signal

• Treat AI tooling (Claude Code and friends) as a first-class part of how you work, not a side experiment

• Enable you to learn from analysts, data scientists, engineers, and responders responsible for various components of Expel's product and services

• Provide access to popular EDR, network, SIEM, identity, and cloud technologies well beyond the Microsoft stack

• Challenge you to push the boundaries of our security vision

What you can do for Expel

• Own our detection coverage across Defender XDR, Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, Azure, and Microsoft 365 — from raw signal through to shipped, tuned detections

• Build and maintain a living map of Microsoft security signal: what exists, known ingestion lag, where it lands, what gates it, how long it's kept, and how far you can trust it

• Track how that signal changes and turn every material change into a concrete action — catching drift before it costs us efficacy

• Tell us where Microsoft's native detections are strong enough to lean on, where they're noisy or shallow, and where Expel needs its own layer

• Make SOC analysts faster by automating Microsoft-specific investigative workflows against the Graph, Defender, Sentinel, and Entra APIs

• Partner with Engineering on our Microsoft integrations — ingestion, API limits and throttling, and schema mapping

• Answer the hard questions from the SOC, CS, and Sales — and mentor the people asking them

• Help customers understand what they're actually covered for, what they're missing, and what turning it on would buy them

What you should bring with you

• Deep, current, hands-on knowledge of the Microsoft security stack — Defender XDR (Endpoint, Identity, Office 365, Cloud Apps), Entra ID, Sentinel, Microsoft Graph, and the Azure and Microsoft 365 control and data planes

• Fluency in KQL: you can write, read, optimize, and debug non-trivial hunting queries across both Defender Advanced Hunting and Sentinel, and you know how and why the two schemas differ

• Working knowledge of the Graph and Graph Security APIs, the Defender and Sentinel APIs, and their authentication, permission, versioning, and throttling models

• A strong grasp of the Entra ID (and legacy Active Directory) identity attack surface — authentication flows, conditional access, OAuth application consent, token theft and replay, hybrid identity and sync, privileged role abuse — and the telemetry each produces

• Solid understanding of Windows internals and command line tooling, with enough macOS and Linux to keep up with Defender's cross-platform coverage

• Experience writing, deploying, and tuning custom detections against Microsoft data sets, plus enough non-Microsoft exposure (AWS, GCP, other EDR and SIEM) to keep perspective

• Proficiency with Python and Sigma, and real fluency using Anthropic tools such as Claude Code to work across systems and data (locally, via MCP, and so on)

• 5+ years in information technology or security operations, with substantial time spent defending or operating Microsoft environments

• Excellent tact and diplomacy skills — you can explain Microsoft's limits to an audience that doesn't want to hear about them

• SC-200, AZ-500, or SC-300 are a plus; demonstrated depth matters considerably more

Work Location

Our headquarters is in Herndon, Virginia. However, we realize that while there is a benefit to in-person interaction, good people don’t all live in Northern Virginia. Remote work is an option for this role.

Additional Notes

The base salary range for this role is between $142,900 USD and $207,200 USD + bonus eligibility and equity. While the full salary band reflects our long-term compensation framework, we're primarily targeting candidates between $160,000 and $192,000 based on experience, skills, and market data.

We believe in paying transparently and equitably. Your salary will ultimately be based on factors such as your experience, skills, team equity, and market data. You’ll also be eligible for unlimited PTO (which we model and encourage), work location flexibility, up to 24 weeks of parental leave, and really excellent health benefits.

We’re only hiring those authorized to work in the United States. We do not currently sponsor immigration visas.

We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer: You’ll receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.

We’ll ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please let us know if you need accommodation of any kind.

listing.description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

Edge Functions are server-side TypeScript functions, distributed globally at the edge - close to your users. They power use cases such as webhook receivers, AI inferences, OG image generation and real-time bots (Slack, Discord, etc). Built on top of Supabase Edge Runtime: an open-source, Deno-based runtime written in Rust that runs JavaScript, TypeScript, and WASM services.

We want developers to be able to build truly global applications by distributing both compute and data globally. Infrastructure concerns like regions, cold starts, CPU and memory provisioning should fade into the background so developers can focus on iterating on business logic.

We are looking for experienced and passionate engineers to help us go further in this vision.

What You’ll Own

•

Evolving Supabase Edge Runtime - an Open-sourced Rust-based host that runs the Deno isolate, manages the main/user runtime split, and enforces per-request memory and CPU limits.

•

Implementing monitoring, alerting, and OpenTelemetry tracing across the runtime, then using that visibility to drive optimizations that improve latency and reliability of the service.

•

Working closely with the Deno and other open-source teams, contributing to upstream and relaying our users' requirements.

•

Participating in an on-call rotation to keep Edge Functions healthy in production.

•

Help manage and improve features like scheduled functions, background tasks, WebSockets streaming, ephemeral file storage, and custom routing.

•

Integrating functions more tightly with the rest of the Supabase stack - Auth, Postgres, Storage, and Realtime.

•

Expanding functions to support more use cases (AI inference, MCP servers, hosting simple websites, URL shorteners).

•

Improving the DX of developing and debugging functions locally through the Supabase CLI, including DevTools integration, logging, and production parity.

What You’ll Bring

•

At least 5 years of backend or systems engineering experience, with strong fluency in Rust and TypeScript.

•

Experience with V8 Isolates, Deno and the JavaScript runtimes in general.

•

Experience operating infrastructure at scale - Kubernetes, AWS, Cloudflare Workers, Redis, or comparable systems.

•

A strong vision for how compute and data can be pushed to the edge.

•

Bonus: experience building developer-facing CLIs or front-end tooling that sits on top of an infrastructure product.

What We Offer

•

Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•

ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•

Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•

Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•

Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•

Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•

Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•

~400 team members

•

60+ countries

•

20+ languages spoken

•

Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•

540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.

Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.

The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.

This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.

You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.

What You'll Be Responsible For

In this role, you'll:

•

Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.

•

Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.

•

Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.

•

Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.

•

Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.

•

Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

•

Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion.

•

Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim.

How You'll Think

Recursive Thinking

You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix.

The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which means the suite has to be right in a way the agent does not, and the thing that grades has to be graded too.

Inversion Thinking

You start from the failure and work backward to the design. The rule is that an agent may never autonomously write a commitment into a shared work system. The weak implementation is an instruction in a prompt. The strong one is that the credential in the agent's tool grant physically cannot set an owner, a due date or a status, so no amount of clever input, prompt injection or model error produces the forbidden write. You reach for the second one first.

Same for evaluation. Before writing a suite you enumerate how the agent can be wrong: an update that invents progress that did not happen, one that quotes a private channel into a public digest, one that is accurate and reads as an accusation, one that credits the wrong person. Then the suite is that list, each case caught before the agent ships rather than after it embarrasses someone.

AI-Native Execution

You use agentic tools on real work, in files and repositories, with the same rigor you apply to anything else you ship. You have a setup of your own and can describe it mechanically: what triggers it, what it is allowed to touch, where the human approves, what it logs, and how you found out the one time it went wrong.

That experience is this job, generalized. You are building for async engineers across 40+ countries who will judge the platform by whether it saves them an hour or costs them one, so you are your own first user and your own harshest reviewer.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

Must Have

•

Have shipped production LLM agent systems that other people depended on. Not demos, not internal showcases. Systems with operational history, real users and at least one incident you can talk through. Prompt engineering on its own does not clear this bar.

•

Design evaluations, not spot checks. You build golden sets, write behavioral assertions, define judge rubrics, set pass thresholds and gate CI on the result. You can explain why "we reviewed a bunch of outputs and they looked good" is not evaluation.

•

Have done deep API work against the systems work actually lives in, and have authored MCP servers. You know the specific failure modes of those APIs, not just that they exist.

•

Own infrastructure end to end in Python on GCP, with a cloud warehouse and infrastructure as code. You provision, deploy, monitor and roll back your own systems, and you close architecture decisions rather than routing them onward.

•

Have taste about how software contacts humans. You treat every notification as spending a limited amount of trust.

Strong Signal

•

Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite.

•

LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on.

listing.description:
QuickMail is a cold email and LinkedIn outreach platform for markets you can't afford to burn. Our customers can't easily replace leads that land in spam, which is why deliverability matters more to us than anything else. We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢.

The Role

We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality.

You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to.

Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are.

The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking.

This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer.

We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it.

If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you.

What Work Looks Like

You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable.

Every day

• Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it.

• Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution.

• Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform.

Delighting customers

• Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success.

• Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked.

• Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates.

Making support smarter with AI

• Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off.

• Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do.

• Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving.

Keeping the product solid

• Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected.

• Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors.

• Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice.

Running the week

• Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated.

• Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps.

Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude.

Who You Are

• You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls.

• You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things.

• You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding.

• You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom.

• Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said.

• You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity.

• You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results.

• You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack.

• Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive.

• Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are.

A Plus If You Have

• Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role.

• Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps.

• Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client.

• Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report.

• An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment.

How We Work Together

You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer.

Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice:

• Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask.

• Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt.

• Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked.

• The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on.

• The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you.

This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once.

Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too.

Benefits

• Contract type: full-time or part-time

• Compensation: $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience and location. US-based hires will work as independent contractors (1099).

• Start date: negotiable

If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: [email]. Please include your full name, the role you're applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process. We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

How We'll Take Care of You:

Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.

Pay Range

$212,000—$265,000 USD

Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @airbnb.com or @ext.airbnb.com email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing. We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Postgres Deployment Engineer to join our PostgreSQL team and help elevate our PostgreSQL offerings.

You’ll work closely with the PostgreSQL team, playing an instrumental role in technical decision-making and refining internal methodologies. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions.

The focus of this role is owning the stability and deployment of our products. You will act as a bridge between product and infrastructure teams to improve the reliability of deployments and upgrades. You will have co-responsibility for builds and deployments via our public supabase/postgres GitHub repository, which bundles features into Docker images and AWS AMIs for cloud and local use.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

•

Package software into our supabase/postgres repo using Nix (with flakes), and help us transition our packaging from traditional to Nix packaging more over time.

•

Manage PostgreSQL lifecycles, ensuring timely major, minor, and extension upgrades.

•

Expand platform release systems to allow developers to increasingly self-service.

•

Optimize CI/CD and tooling, specifically expanding GitHub Actions, team tooling, and testing/release approaches.

•

Resolve production issues by proactively identifying and fixing problems in customer deployments.

•

Maintain best practices and tests to ensure enhanced stability and decreased deployment risks.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

•

Have 3+ years of experience with PostgreSQL and its ecosystem, including extensions and performance optimization.

•

Are an Infrastructure Expert with proven experience in management, tooling, and optimization.

•

Are proficient in the Nix package management system (including flakes) alongside Ansible, Packer, Docker, QEMU/KVM, AWS, and Kubernetes.

•

Have experience building for multiple architectures, specifically Linux and Darwin/macOS aarch64 targets.

•

Are comfortable with polyglot environments, including builds for C/C++, Go, JavaScript, and Rust-based projects.

•

Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences, especially when interacting with customers.

•

Have experience in async or globally distributed teams and value independent, proactive problem-solving.

•

Are willing to mentor, taking on responsibility for teaching the engineering team to use and contribute to our Nix-based work.

What We Offer

•

Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•

ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•

Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•

Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•

Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•

Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•

Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•

~400 team members

•

60+ countries

•

20+ languages spoken

•

Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•

540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Mercury is building a complete finance stack for startups. We work hard to create the easiest and safest banking* experience possible to simplify entrepreneurs' and business owners’ financial lives.The challenge is to do so while ensuring we protect Mercury, customers and the broader financial ecosystem from bad actors and harmful, illegal or unauthorized activities.

Our AML Investigations team is crucial in this mission and is responsible for detecting suspicious activity, conducting thorough investigations, and shutting down bad actors. This team is growing and we’re looking to hire an additional AML Risk Investigator to help us with Bank Partner Requests for Information, Transaction Monitoring, Financial Crime Investigations, Case Management and drafting Unusual Activity Reports. As a member of our Investigations team, you’ll help handle our transaction monitoring queues while balancing an eagle eye for risk with excellent user experience. To begin with, you’ll work to help make sure we have smart, risk-based monitoring in place and help build out our case management technology and processes.

You’ll need to learn how a really wide range of businesses work and bring your knowledge to bear on our processes and product. Some of this work is repetitive and requires close attention to detail, so we need someone who loves working fraud and anti-money laundering transaction queues and managing a variety of complex investigations.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

• Provide input as we implement new transaction monitoring rules and tune existing ones

• Contact our users for information on their account usage and transactions

• Work with our partners and internal team members to review and assess information received from users

About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We are seeking a Platform Software Engineer with deep experience in distributed systems to help design, build, and maintain core platform services. You will work primarily in TypeScript and Go to deliver reliable, scalable, and secure systems that power Supabase at massive scale.

What you'll be doing:

•

Design and implement distributed services and APIs that power the Supabase Platform.

•

Lead projects that improve scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency across existing systems.

•

Build data-intensive workflows, background jobs, and event-driven pipelines.

•

Own service SLIs/SLOs and collaborate on incident response and post-incident reviews.

•

Improve system observability with metrics, logging, tracing, and profiling.

•

Contribute to our CI/CD and release processes to ship safely and quickly.

•

Partner with product teams to deliver features end-to-end, from design docs to production.

•

Write clear design documents, RFCs, and high-quality tests.

What we're looking for:

•

Experienced in designing and operating distributed systems, with strong foundations in consistency, fault tolerance, partitioning, consensus, and back pressure.

•

Proficient in TypeScript and/or Go, ideally with 5+ years building production services in one or both languages (other languages also considered).

•

Comfortable with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred) and container orchestration.

•

Familiar with multi-tenant architectures, API design, and data modelling.

•

Knowledgeable about networking fundamentals and security best practices.

•

Experienced with Infrastructure as Code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine).

•

Comfortable participating in on-call rotations for large-scale production systems.

Nice to have:

•

Experience with Postgres internals, logical replication, or CDC pipelines.

•

Experience with service meshes, workload identity, or zero-trust networking.

•

Background in performance engineering and capacity planning.

•

Open source contributions in systems, databases, or runtime tooling.

What We Offer

•

Fully Remote

We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

•

ESOP

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

•

Tech Allowance

Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

•

Health Benefits

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

•

Annual Off-Sites

Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

•

Flexible Work

We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

•

Professional Development

Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

•

~400 team members

•

60+ countries

•

20+ languages spoken

•

Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

•

540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

We are hiring a Head of Technology for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.

Original job posting link

About garden3d

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

Weâre the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer weâre building a different type of technology shop â one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and weâve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

Weâre building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Index - Community

Index is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.

We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.

garden3d TK â Media

At garden3d, weâre in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone
Mill
IngredientAI

â°ï ̧ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

ï ̧ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

Responsibilities

Infrastructure & Network Management

· Infrastructure and Server Management

• Plan, operate, and continuously improve the University’s data center, Windows Server environment, Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, file services, print servers, storage, virtualization, backup, and disaster recovery systems.
• Maintain availability, capacity, performance, patching, monitoring, and lifecycle plans for critical infrastructure.
• Network and Campus Wi‐Fi
• Manage secure, resilient LAN, WAN, internet, VPN, VLAN, routing, switching, firewall, and campus-wide Wi‐Fi services across academic, administrative, residential, and public areas.
• Monitor coverage, bandwidth, uptime, and user experience; maintain network diagrams, configurations, and escalation procedures.
• Cloud and Identity Services
• Administer Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace (G Suite), including user provisioning, email, collaboration, storage, licensing, security settings, single sign-on, and multi-factor authentication.
• Integrate cloud services with on-premises systems while maintaining appropriate access controls and data protection.

Access Control and Surveillance Systems

• Manage and maintain the University’s electronic access control, CCTV, video management, recording, monitoring, and related security systems across campuses and facilities.
• Administer user access permissions, cards, credentials, system integrations, retention settings, audit logs, and authorized access to surveillance footage in accordance with university policies and applicable privacy requirements.
• Coordinate preventive maintenance, fault resolution, upgrades, incident support, documentation, and vendor performance to ensure reliable system availability and coverage.

2. University Systems, ERP & Digital Platforms

· University ERP and Academic Systems

• Oversee the University ERP and related student information, admissions, registration, examination, finance, HR, library, learning management, and reporting systems.
• Manage roles, permissions, workflows, integrations, upgrades, data quality, vendor support, and business continuity.
• Work with academic and administrative departments to translate operational requirements into secure and practical solutions.

· Website and Digital Channels

• Ensure the University website, portals, domains, hosting, SSL certificates, backups, accessibility, performance, and security are properly managed.
• Provide technical governance and access control for official social media accounts and coordinate with authorized communications staff; content ownership remains with the designated department.

Data and Integration

• Maintain secure data exchange, reporting, retention, and recovery processes across institutional systems.
• Support database administration, audit trails, and accurate management information while protecting confidential student and employee records.

3. Cybersecurity, Privacy, Risk & Continuity

• Develop and enforce the University’s cybersecurity policies, standards, incident-response procedures, acceptable-use rules, access controls, and security-awareness program.
• Protect networks, endpoints, servers, cloud services, ERP data, laboratories, websites, email, and privileged accounts using layered controls including firewalls, endpoint protection, filtering, MFA, logging, vulnerability management, and timely patching.
• Conduct risk assessments, access reviews, backup validation, restoration tests, disaster recovery exercises, and incident investigations; report material risks and incidents to university leadership.
• Support compliance with applicable data-protection, records-management, licensing, audit, and higher-education requirements.
• Maintain business continuity plans for critical academic and administrative services, with documented recovery priorities and responsibilities.

4. Computer Laboratories, End-User Services & Service Management

· Computer Laboratories

• Manage computer laboratories, classroom technology, specialized academic software, hardware standards, images, licensing, maintenance schedules, internet access, printing, and readiness for teaching and examinations.
• Coordinate with faculty to forecast software and hardware requirements before each semester and ensure compliant deployment.

User Support

• Deliver responsive support to students and staff through effective helpdesk, ticketing, escalation, and service-level management processes.
• Oversee desktops, laptops, peripherals, audio-visual equipment, print services, email, accounts, and remote-access support.

Documentation and Training

• Maintain SOPs, inventories, configuration records, knowledge articles, and user guides.
• Provide staff and student orientation, cybersecurity awareness, and practical training on institutional systems.

5. IT Strategy, Governance, Projects & Budget

• Prepare and execute the University’s IT strategy, annual operating plan, technology roadmap, policies, standards, risk register, and budget.
• Lead infrastructure upgrades, ERP improvements, cloud adoption, laboratory refreshes, migrations, security initiatives, and other IT projects from requirements through implementation and handover.
• Define scope, schedule, cost, quality, risks, procurement needs, and success measures; provide clear progress reports to management.
• Establish governance for architecture, change management, data ownership, project prioritization, and technology procurement.

6. Vendor, Contract & Asset Management

• Manage sourcing, contracts, renewals, service-level agreements, ISP relationships, software licensing, warranties, and vendor performance.
• Maintain accurate hardware and software inventories and manage the full asset lifecycle from specification and acquisition through deployment, maintenance, secure disposal, and replacement planning.
• Ensure purchases are technically fit for purpose, standardized where appropriate, cost-effective, supportable, secure, and compliant with university procurement requirements.

7. IT Team Leadership & University Collaboration

• Lead, organize, and develop the IT team; define roles, schedules, priorities, performance objectives, on-call arrangements, documentation standards, and professional-development plans.
